research.query: Why are flames spherical in space?
research.answer:
**Evidence**
- ACME CFI-G: 1. Steady-state cool diffusion flames on spherical porous burners. [S1]
- ACME/Flame Design: 3. Steady-state spherical diffusion flames are possible. [S2]
- ACME/Flame Design: The kinetics and warm flame chemistry associated with radiative extinction of spherical diffusion flames; Soot Formation in Spherical Diffusion Flames; On the existence of steady-state gaseous microgravity spherical diffusion flames in the presence of radiation heat loss;… [S3]
- ACME CFI-G: Spherical gas-fueled cool diffusion flames; Cool diffusion flames in a stably stratified stagnation flow [S4]
- ACME s-Flame: Structure and response of spherical diffusion flames, including near-extinction behaviour. [S5]
- BASS-II maps solid-fuel burning down to 13.6 % O2: BASS-II ran 129 tests with initial O2 between 13.6 and 22.2 % vol, mostly on PMMA, SIBAL (cotton-fiberglass fabric), Nomex. Flow annotations record extinction in 15 tests, blow-off in 3 and no ignition in 1. Limitation: Outcome annotations  [S10]
- 1-g material screening is not automatically conservative: Spacecraft material selection relies on NASA-STD-6001 Test 1, which ranks materials by 1-g behaviour. BASS and BASS-II were built on the hypothesis that, with adequate ventilation, materials burn as well if not better in microgravity than i [S11]

- Extractive answer (no language model configured): passages are quoted, not interpreted.
- Only documents in this knowledge base were searched.

sources.title: Cool flames: combustion at 500–1000 K
sources.text: Cool diffusion flames have peak temperatures of about 500–1000 K. FLEX, CFI and CFI-G studied them on droplets and burners in microgravity. Limitation: Research fuels and configurations; relevance to cabin fires is an open question, not a finding.

top_passage.text: The E-FIELD Flames research is not being conducted to serve any space applications, but it is possible that its findings could aid the development of future space-based combustion devices (e.g., for solid waste processing). The use of electric fields to control flames can reduce the production of harmful pollutants in practical terrestrial combustion. The combustion of fossil fuel is the primary human source of greenhouse gas and acid rain and furthermore creates soot, which can be beneficial but is also a health hazard. Combustion using electrical fields may also allow for more efficient combustion, reducing fuel consumption in addition to unwanted emissions.

results.title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II
why: Data: 9 test-level records.

top_passage.text: The Saffire-II experiment provides a new way to study a realistic fire on an exploration vehicle, which has not been possible in the past because the risks are too high. Instruments on an unmanned cargo vessel measure oxygen, carbon dioxide, heat, pressure and flame growth, and two video cameras provide views of the flame. Results determine microgravity flammability limits for several spacecraft materials, help to validate NASA’s material selection criteria, and how microgravity and limited oxygen affect flame size. The investigation is crucial for the safety of current and future space missions.
